title: Replate Backend API — Request/Response Payload Schemas (Phase 1)

JobStatus.description: The pipeline runs in two stages. Queued/Processing = stage 1 (identify restaurant, fetch menu, vision guess, menu match). Identified = stage 1 done: the dish is auto-saved to the cookbook with a match and confidence outcome, but has no recipe - a terminal state until the user asks for one. Generating = stage 2 (recipe generation) running after POST /jobs/{jobId}/reverse-engineer. Completed = recipe available. Failed means stage 1 failed; a stage-2 failure reverts to Identified instead. Cancelled means the user aborted an in-flight scan via POST /jobs/{jobId}/cancel to stop model spend - a normal terminal state, kept distinct from Failed.

FailureCode.description: Why a Failed job failed, when the client needs to tell cases apart. not_food = the photo is not a dish, caught by the upload-time food pre-check or by the vision step's is_food gate. Mirrors backend shared/models.FailureCode.

MatchMethod.description: The anti-hallucination signal: whether the dish was cross-checked against the restaurant's real menu, or is vision-only guesswork.

RateLimitedResponse.description: 429 body. Sent with a Retry-After header carrying the same number of seconds. Scanning and recipe generation have separate quotas - see docs/api.md.

role.description: e.g. Protein, Sauce, Side, Garnish, Component

JobSummary.description: One item in the GET /jobs list response - no ingredients/steps, just enough for a list row/card.

image_url.description: Freshly re-signed read-only SAS URL, valid for SAS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_MINUTES.

POST /jobs.description: Reserves an upload slot and creates the job row. Does NOT start the pipeline - POST /jobs/{jobId}/uploaded does, once the photo is actually in Blob Storage.

body.description: Exactly one of the two location sources - GPS coordinates (device location for a live capture, or the photo's EXIF for an upload), or a manually-selected restaurant when an uploaded photo has no EXIF GPS. Supplying both, or neither, is a 400.

upload_url.description: Short-lived, write-only presigned S3 URL. Client PUTs photo bytes directly to S3 with it. No special headers required.

image_key.description: S3 object key (uploads/<uuid>.jpg) the job was created against. Stored server-side; returned for traceability.

POST /jobs/{jobId}/uploaded.auth: X-Debug-User-Oid header required; must match the job's owner
POST /jobs/{jobId}/uploaded.description: Signals that the PUT to upload_url finished, which is what starts stage 1. POST /jobs cannot do this itself: the client only uploads after that call returns the SAS URL, so enqueuing there raced the upload and the orchestrator could read the blob before it existed. No request body.

200.description: The upload-time food pre-check (Rekognition DetectLabels) found nothing food-like in the photo. The job is already "Failed" and was never queued. Any uncertain or failed check falls through to the 202 path instead.

409.description: The job is past "Queued" - its photo was already submitted. Makes the call safe to retry.

GET /jobs/{jobId}.auth: X-Debug-User-Oid header required; must match the job's owner

image_url.description: Freshly re-signed read-only SAS URL, re-minted on every call.

error_message.description: Present whenever the job has one. On a "Failed" job, why stage 1 failed. On an "Identified" job, why a previous reverse-engineer attempt failed - the action stays retryable.

failure_code.description: Present on some "Failed" jobs so the client can choose its copy without parsing error_message.

result.description: Present from "Identified" onward, not only when "Completed" - the matched dish, restaurant and confidence badge are available before any recipe exists. "elements" is an empty array until stage 2 has run.

POST /jobs/{jobId}/reverse-engineer.auth: X-Debug-User-Oid header required; must match the job's owner
POST /jobs/{jobId}/reverse-engineer.description: Starts stage 2 - generating the per-element ingredients and method. Only runs on explicit request because it is the heaviest and most expensive call in the pipeline. No request body.

409.description: The job is not in the "Identified" state - covers stage 1 not finished, generation already in flight, and a recipe already generated. Also returned for jobs created before the pipeline was split, which have no stored vision analysis.

429.description: The caller's recipe-generation quota is spent. The job stays "Identified" so it can be retried once the window reopens.

PATCH /jobs/{jobId}/save.auth: X-Debug-User-Oid header required; must match the job's owner
PATCH /jobs/{jobId}/save.description: Sets saved state. Jobs are auto-saved into the cookbook when stage 1 completes, so this is now mainly how a dish is removed.

GET /profile.description: The caller's profile. Created lazily on first read, so a new user gets null display_name/email.

PUT /profile.description: Updates the caller's display name. email is the sign-in identity and is not editable here; profile photo is not yet supported.

display_name.description: Trimmed before validation; blank or over 80 chars is a 400.

GET /restaurants/search.description: Restaurant name typeahead backing the manual-selection flow, used when an uploaded photo has no EXIF GPS. Backed by OpenStreetMap Nominatim server-side; no API key required. A place_id returned here is what goes into POST /jobs's selected_restaurant.

query.description: Required. Blank or whitespace-only is a 400.

latitude.description: Optional. Only biases result ranking - not a hard filter, and never becomes the job's location. Applied only when longitude is also supplied.

502.description: The Nominatim service was unreachable or returned an error status.
